newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Nov 27.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.
-- Government sources are cited as saying truck drivers and employers reached the preliminary stages of an agreement this morning. A French truckers' strike is in its tenth day.

-- President's office denies any knowledge of an alleged secret document reporting conversations between two GEC bosses over the advantages GEC would gain from a takeover of Thomson by Alcatel Alsthom, their 50-50 venture partner in GEC-Alsthom. The government last month said it preferred a competing bid for Thomson by Lagardere.
-- Labour unrest and rumours of political reshuffling worry investors. Franc fell one centime against the mark yesterday.
-- Usinor-Sacilor subsidiary Unimetal expected to post 1996 loss of around 500 million francs.

-- Finance minister says UAP vice chairman Didier Pfeiffer will be appointed new chairman of state-owned insurer GAN, replacing Jean-Jacques Bonnaud. The cabinet approved a decree firing Bonnaud this morning.
-- Eurotunnel hopes to resume passenger traffic next week, says tunnel repairs from fire may take up to six months.
-- Computer manufacturer Compagnie des Machines Bull to be privatised before the end of December.
-- A planned merger between Framatome and GEC-Alsthom may jeopardise Franco-German cooperation in nuclear sector, according to experts' report on planned merger commissioned by unions.
